record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.original_question: What cohomology theory correctly parametrizes deformations of noncompact complex manifolds, with the property that vanishing of this cohomology forces all deformations to be trivial?

evidence.quote: Question 20. What is the correct cohomology theory that parametrizes deformations of noncompact manifolds? (Vanishing of such a cohomology should imply existence of only trivial deformations.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a noncompact complex manifold. In the classical Kodaira–Spencer theory of deformations of compact complex manifolds, infinitesimal deformations of the complex structure are parametrized by $H^1(X, T_X)$, and the vanishing $H^1(X, T_X) = 0$ implies rigidity (every small deformation is trivial). For noncompact $X$, this correspondence fails in general: $H^1(X, T_X)$ need not parametrize deformations correctly, and its vanishing need not force triviality of deformations (especially when one allows the underlying smooth type to vary in the family).

Identify (or construct) a cohomology theory $\mathcal{H}^*(X)$ — defined naturally for noncompact complex manifolds $X$, possibly taking into account behavior at infinity (e.g., on a chosen compactification $\overline{X}$ with boundary divisor $D = \overline{X} \setminus X$) — with the following two properties:

1. (Parametrization) The first group $\mathcal{H}^1(X)$ is in natural bijection with isomorphism classes of (suitably defined) infinitesimal deformations of the complex structure of $X$.

2. (Rigidity) The vanishing $\mathcal{H}^1(X) = 0$ implies that every deformation of $X$ in the appropriate category is trivial.

Determine such a cohomology theory and prove that it satisfies both properties.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on deformations of noncompact complex manifolds (e.g., on noncompact surfaces, log-deformation theory, and compactifiable manifolds) shows that classical $H^1(X,T_X)$ is insufficient: cohomological rigidity does not imply absence of deformations, and various candidate cohomologies (logarithmic tangent sheaf cohomology on a compactification, $L^2$-cohomology, Dolbeault-type groups) have been studied for special cases, but no single, generally accepted cohomology theory has been established that parametrizes deformations of arbitrary noncompact complex manifolds and whose vanishing forces triviality. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Deformations of noncompact manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses semiuniversal families and notes that for noncompact manifolds H^1(X,T_X)=0 may not imply rigidity when the smooth type varies.
status_evidence.claim: Standard tangent-sheaf cohomology fails to control deformations of noncompact complex manifolds in general.

status_evidence.title: Obstructions of deforming complex structures and cohomology contractions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent investigation into cohomological obstruction theories for complex structure deformations.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research is still seeking the right cohomological framework for deformations beyond the classical compact case.
